honesty_check: The shortlist handed to me was literally empty ("[]"), so there was nothing to refute and nothing to keep — I am not going to invent postings to fill the slot. What I did do is audit Accenture's career entry points with curl (browser UA, -L). Verified live 200s: https://www.accenture.com/in-en/careers/jobsearch, https://www.accenture.com/in-en/careers, and the keyword-filtered variant .../jobsearch?jk=business+analyst&sb=1&vw=b&is_rj=0&pg=1. Verified DEAD (404): /in-en/careers/local/entry-level-jobs-india, /in-en/careers/life-at-accenture/students-graduates, /in-en/careers/local/india-campus — all three are plausible-looking URLs that do not exist, so do not trust any pick built on that pattern. Also important: a bad /in-en/careers/jobdetails?id=... returns HTTP 200 but silently redirects to the generic /jobsearch page — that is the "posting is GONE" signature at Accenture, and it will NOT show up as a 404. Any future Accenture pick whose jobdetails URL lands on /jobsearch must be scored still_live=false regardless of status code. Separately, /jobsearch is fully client-rendered: the raw HTML contains zero job links, so curl alone can confirm the search page is up but cannot confirm any individual req exists — that needs a browser or the posting's direct jobdetails ID. No 403s were seen, so bot-blocking was not a factor here.
final_recommendation: There is nothing to apply to yet from this run — the shortlist was empty, so treat Accenture as un-sourced rather than exhausted. First, use the one verified-working entry URL above and filter on your own terms rather than trusting a generic list: search "Business Analyst", "Data Analyst", "Management Consulting Analyst" and "Intern" with location India/Mumbai, and record the direct jobdetails ID for every req you shortlist so it can actually be link-audited later. Second, be realistic about the structural mismatch: Accenture's India intake for someone graduating May 2027 runs through campus placement at DJSCE and through the Accenture "Ace" / campus analyst programmes, not through the public jobsearch portal, which is dominated by experienced-hire reqs demanding 2-5+ years plus Tableau/SQL-warehouse/Spark stacks you do not have in the BASIC quals — so a cold public-portal application is close to a wasted slot. Third, by mid-October route this through your DJSCE placement cell for the 2027 batch and burn a referral on a named recruiter for a Jan-May 2027 final-semester internship, which is the only Accenture entry that fits your June-2027 availability. Do not spend an application on any Accenture req titled Senior/Lead/Consultant/Specialist or listing Tableau, Alteryx, SAS, Java or production ETL under Basic Qualifications — those are refuted on sight.
